evidence.summary: Increasing age from 25 to 75 increased the score substantially. With loan_amount 25, the score increased from 0.2604 to 0.7139. With loan_amount 75, it increased from 0.3221 to 0.8075.
Increasing loan_amount from 25 to 75 increased the score. At age 25, the score increased from 0.2604 to 0.3221. At age 75, it increased from 0.7139 to 0.8075.
Both age and loan_amount increase the score. The effect of loan_amount is slightly stronger at higher age, indicating a positive interaction between age and loan_amount.
Changing income from 25 to 75 produced no score change when loan_amount was fixed at 25 or 75. This suggests income has no observable effect under these tested conditions.
